story_of_day.headline: Democrats take both chambers: a blue wave
story_of_day.story: Democrats won control of the House and the Senate, flipping Senate seats in Texas, Iowa, Kansas, North Carolina, South Carolina and Ohio, and unseating Susan Collins in Maine. Voters punished Trump, and he has acknowledged the Iran conflict played a role in the defeat. Expect two years of fights over the budget, investigations and the limits of presidential power.
story_of_day.so_what: Trump keeps control of foreign policy, but Congress can now cut funding, hold hearings and slow his agenda. Markets are already trading on it: the dollar fell and AI and renewables are in focus.

last_time.text: Last run, polls were open with record turnout in several states and the results were still unknown. Now the result is in: a full Democratic sweep, bigger than the 'House only' outcome many were planning for.

story_of_day.money_angle: The dollar index hit a one-month low (about 101.3), gold is near $4,055 (up from about $3,918 on Tuesday morning) and Treasuries rallied. Renewable stocks jumped in Asia and Europe, while AI names face the risk of tougher regulation.

my_take.text: Don't chase the 'blue trade' in renewables after a one-day gap. If you want exposure, wait for a pullback and size it small.
my_take.reasoning: Election-night jumps often fade once reality sets in. Democrats now hold Congress, but Trump still has the veto, so new energy or AI law is unlikely to pass before 2029. What changes now is oversight and spending fights, not legislation.
my_take.wrong_if: Renewables keep climbing for a week with no pullback, which would mean the market is pricing in something lasting, such as a deal on energy credits.

cards.headline: Four tankers hit mines near Hormuz
cards.story: Iran's Revolutionary Guards say four oil tankers were destroyed by naval mines south of the Strait of Hormuz, in an area Tehran declared off-limits, and two other ships were seized. Iran's chief negotiator Ghalibaf said Americans voted 'no to war', and Tehran says it won't reopen the Strait until Washington lifts its blockade and halts attacks.
cards.so_what: Talks are still alive, but both sides are using the election to harden positions. Shipping risk in the Gulf is rising, not falling.

last_time.text: Last run Trump said US aid to Israel would end this year and Tehran dismissed reports of progress. Since then the Iranian side has leaned on the US vote result and the mine attacks have escalated the standoff.

cards.money_angle: Brent is about $101.6, below the $105.92 it traded at on Tuesday morning despite the tanker news.

cards.headline: Moscow hopes the US vote won't change Ukraine talks
cards.story: The Kremlin says it hopes the midterm result won't disturb Trump's 'peacemaking efforts' on Ukraine. In Brussels, the European Commission is hosting talks on support for Ukraine with the US, France, Germany, Britain, NATO and the World Bank.
cards.so_what: A Democratic Congress is likely to be friendlier to Ukraine aid, which gives Kyiv and Europe more room. Russia wants to keep the talks in Trump's hands.

last_time.text: Last run Russian strikes on an aid centre, a hospice and a hospital killed at least 38 people, and Zelensky hoped for Abu Dhabi talks. Now the focus has shifted to how Washington's politics affect the diplomacy.

cards.headline: Wage board meets as garment unrest drags on
cards.story: The garment wage protests are now in their second week. The BGMEA reports disruption at 529 factories, and the government has put 24 platoons of border guards into industrial areas. The Minimum Wage Board has started discussing proposed pay rates, and a report says workers could get higher pay from January. Meanwhile, October exports rose 4.4% to nearly $4bn.
cards.so_what: Exports are holding up for now, but a wage deal that feels too small keeps the streets angry, and one that feels too big squeezes the low-cost edge buyers pay for.

last_time.text: Last run almost 1,000 factories were reported closed, with arrests in Mirpur. The count is lower in this report (529 disrupted) and the focus has moved to the wage board, which is the first real step toward a settlement.

watch.title: Wage board decision and Hormuz
watch.text: Watch whether Bangladesh's wage board announces a figure that calms the factories, and whether Brent reacts to the tanker attacks or keeps drifting down.

takes_review.text: Brent was $105.92 when I said don't chase oil. It is $101.62 now, still inside my $98-115 range, even with four tankers reported destroyed by mines. No clear winner yet, so the take stands.
